description: The plot illustrates the sparsity ratio of SDPA (Scaled Dot-Product Attention) output across layers, using a threshold of 1e-2, as described in the paper “Gated Attention for Large Language Models: Non-linearity, Sparsity, and Attention-Sink-Free.” The x-axis represents the layer index, ranging from 0 to approximately 23, with tick marks at intervals of 5. The y-axis shows the sparsity ratio, ranging from 0.0 to 1.0 in linear scale, indicating the proportion of SDPA output values falling below the 1e-2 threshold. Three distinct lines are plotted: a blue dashed line labeled “sparsity ratio before gate, avg 0.03,” which remains low and relatively flat across layers, starting near 0.2 and declining slightly to below 0.05; an orange dotted line labeled “sparsity ratio after gate, avg 0.44,” which begins near 1.0 and drops sharply to around 0.2 by layer 10, then fluctuates between 0.15 and 0.4 through layer 23; and a green dash-dotted line labeled “sparsity ratio after average gate, avg 0.33,” which starts near 1.0, declines steeply to about 0.15 by layer 10, then rises slightly and fluctuates between 0.1 and 0.25 through layer 23. The legend also reports average sparsity ratios over all layers for each condition.
